correctness.rationale: Finite-radius aligned-center minimizer exists: positive Bessel Fourier coefficients make the center unique and the Bessel norm grows at large concentration. Under delta=1-r, uniform L2 convergence of rescaled kernels gives exact F(c). Positive Laplace representation makes the stationarity h(x) strictly decreasing from 1 to 0, so F has one strict global minimum. Small and large scaled concentrations are excluded uniformly by norm and cross-term estimates. Every actual minimizer therefore has delta^2*kappa to c*, and normalized minimum error to F*. Moment matching solves a strictly monotone Bessel-ratio equation and chooses the wrong scale. Standard-library checker replays finite diagnostics; infinite claims are supported by proof, not by tests.

value.rationale: For the natural task of replacing a Poisson circular smoother by one von-Mises smoother, the exact sharp concentrated-limit fitting scale differs by an entire power of 1-r from canonical moment matching. A universal, uniquely characterized Cauchy–Gaussian constant gives the exact 14.17054-fold asymptotic squared-error penalty for moment matching. This supplies a motivated parameter-calibration boundary useful when substituting circular smoothing families, rather than a routine numerical slice.
